headline: Copilot's IDE completions complement Claude Code's terminal agent — moderate conflict because Copilot does not execute or commit autonomously.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot completions land in editor buffers that Claude Code subsequently reads. A poisoned suggestion accepted by the developer can become a tool-use instruction string in a comment that biases Claude Code's next plan. The pathway exists but requires human acceptance of the completion first.
mitigations: Have Claude Code re-run lint/tests after edits

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both ship code context to vendor backends — Copilot to GitHub, Claude Code to Anthropic. Same source flows to two processors. GitHub Copilot Business does not retain prompts, but the dual-vendor flow is still a finding for compliance review.
mitigations: Use Copilot Business/Enterprise for the no-retention guarantee
Audit which directories Claude Code can read

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot does not execute shell or commit on its own; it only proposes inline edits. Conflict surface is limited to the open buffer being mutated by both agents, which the IDE serializes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot's completion may be ingested by Claude Code as if user-authored, with no signal that it was machine-generated. Claude Code's next step might rationalize a Copilot hallucination instead of catching it.
mitigations: Add a CI step that fails the PR if Claude Code's commit isn't reviewed

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot Business / Enterprise have documented data handling, and Anthropic does not train on Claude Code traffic. Compliance overlap is acceptable in most enterprise reviews.
